summary: Loads 3D point data and point attributes from point-cloud, mesh, floating-point, image, and ASCII table formats into POPs. It maps fields into P, N, Tex, Color, custom attributes, and arrays, with thinning and reranging pages for import cleanup.

key_concepts: Point File In POP loads 3D point data from single files or file sequences and maps file fields into POP attributes.
Default mappings place x/y/z into P and r/g/b/a into Color, but position, normal, texture, color, and custom attribute fields can all be reassigned.
Custom sequential blocks can create float, float2, float3, float4, and array attributes, with optional qualifiers such as color or direction.
ASCII point files share one parser across txt, csv, xyz, and related extensions: delimiter and header handling can determine whether fields map correctly.
The Thin and ReRange pages support import cleanup without building temporary attribute nodes, including point thinning, random seeds, and attribute value remapping.
Gaussian splat files can expose many specialized attributes, so planner output should map only the required fields rather than assuming a compact point-cloud layout.
common_gotchas: ASCII delimiters are auto-detected; malformed headers or inconsistent delimiters can silently map fields poorly.
Gaussian splat files can contain many specialized attributes, so use custom sequential blocks deliberately.
Limit maxpoints for huge files before adding render, proximity, or neighbor stages.
